title: Harira
subtitle: Moroccan lamb, chickpea, and lentil soup
excerpt: The great Moroccan soup: a thick, warming bowl of lamb, chickpeas, lentils, tomatoes, and a fragrant spice mix of cinnamon, ginger, and turmeric, finished with a tart lemon juice and fresh coriander. The traditional soup to break the Ramadan fast.

recipe.sourceNotes: Harira is the national soup of Morocco and one of the most important dishes in Moroccan domestic cooking. It is most strongly associated with Ramadan, when it is traditionally served to break the fast at iftar: the combination of legumes, meat, tomato, and lemon makes it simultaneously nourishing, satisfying, and digestively gentle after a day of fasting. The soup is also eaten at celebrations, weddings, and as everyday winter food. Recipes vary enormously by household and region: the lamb is optional in many versions, the ratio of chickpeas to lentils shifts, and some versions use a flour-and-water mixture (tedouira) to thicken the soup. The characteristic flavour profile — cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, fresh coriander, and lemon — is consistent across virtually all versions and is what makes harira immediately recognisable.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy saucepan or casserole.

content.text: The soup thickens considerably as it cooks; add extra water or stock if it becomes too stiff. A proper harira should be thick (almost porridge-like) rather than thin. Add the lemon juice and fresh coriander at the very end: both lose flavour if cooked for long. Tinned chickpeas are fine here and save significant time.

items.preparation: mixed with 100 ml cold water to make a slurry

content.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb pieces in batches. Remove and set aside. Add the onion and celery and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, turmeric, cumin, and pepper and cook for 1 minute.

Return the lamb to the pan. Add the tinned tomatoes, tomato purée, and 1.5 litres of water. Bring to a boil, then add the red lentils. Simmer for 30 minutes. Add the chickpeas and continue cooking for 30 minutes more.

Stir the flour-and-water slurry into the simmering soup and cook for a further 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the soup has thickened. Season with salt. Remove from the heat and stir in the lemon juice, coriander, and parsley. Serve immediately.
